title: A Field Guide to Slop
summary: What "slopcore" means: plates of AI slop's common species, a key to identify a specimen, and what the "-core" suffix does.

title: The Limbic Blueprint
summary: What the limbic system is, mapped part by part against its nearest AI counterparts, with a rough rating of how far each analogy stretches.

title: WLED Strip Planner
summary: What WLED is and how to plan the power side of an LED strip: a planner for pixel count, supply size, power feeds, wire drop, and frame rate, a wiring diagram drawn to match, and the firmware's vocabulary.

title: Pull the Stops: How a Pipe Organ Speaks
summary: A playable pipe organ console: draw stops, start the blower, and watch which pipes open in the wind chest and which harmonics each stop adds, with the reason organ stops are measured in feet.

title: Time in Range: A Sampling Lab for Home INR Testing
summary: How the INR is built from a clotting time, what a home test strip does with a drop of blood, and a lab where two testing schedules watch the same wandering line and estimate its time in range.

title: One in Twenty: What a Blood Test's Reference Range Means
summary: The common blood panels and what each looks at, where a reference range comes from, and a printer that runs panels on made-up healthy people to show how often they get flagged anyway.

title: One Script to a Pipeline: Six Stages of a Data Pipeline Growing
summary: A made-up data pipeline drawn as a transit line, growing from one nightly script to steps, checks, and save points, with six kinds of bad night to throw at each stage.

title: Five Stations for One Slide: A Pathology Data Pipeline, Run on the Page
style: photographer's contact sheet and grease pencil
summary: One drawn pathology slide run through five stations of a data pipeline: find the tissue, cross out blurred, folded and inked tiles, even out stain colour, and count the tiles that come out.

title: Rows in the Drawer: SQL on a Made-Up Pathology Lab, One Clause at a Time
summary: Six SQL queries run clause by clause on a made-up lab's cases, slides, and scans, each in a first-written and a fixed version, with a SQLite scratchpad for trying more.

title: Same Patient, Both Sides: Why Slide Tiles Are Split by Patient Before a Model Is Scored
summary: Why tiles cut from pathology slides are split by patient before a model is scored: a nearest-neighbour toy that shows the leak, and the same effect one level up, between sites.

title: Tape and Tally: One Day of Scanner Events, Read Live and Read Nightly
summary: One made-up day of slide-scanner events through a partitioned log, a live consumer group with event-time windows, and a nightly batch job: lag, crashes, replays, and late data.
